title: SUBOFF BFL vs Standard BB Drag Comparison

Cd_p.comment: Pressure drag similar across methods (~0.005). BFL slightly lower.

Cd_f.comment: BFL friction drag 2.6x higher than standard BB. BFL places wall at true surface, increasing near-wall velocity gradient. Friction formula (tau=2*nu*u_t) assumes half-way BB wall distance (0.5), not adjusted for BFL q-values.

Cd_tot.comment: Standard BB closest to Cf_ref=0.042 (5.6% error). BFL overestimates by ~155%.

bfl_normal_comparison.comment: BFL from_suboff vs from_gradient differ by <1%. Normal method has minimal impact on drag when q-values are analytical.

key_findings: Standard BB gives Cd_tot=0.0444, closest to Cf_ref=0.042 (5.6% error).
BFL overestimates total drag by ~155% due to 2.6x higher friction drag.
Pressure drag is similar across all methods (~0.005), confirming BFL correctly handles pressure.
BFL from_suboff vs from_gradient differ by <1% — normal method has minimal impact.
BFL q-values: 11842 boundary links, q_mean=0.735 (wall closer to solid cell than half-way).

Root cause: friction drag formula (tau=2*nu*u_t) assumes half-way BB (wall at 0.5 cell distance). BFL places wall at q distance, so near-wall velocity is lower, inflating computed friction. Formula needs q-correction for BFL.
Vectorized BFL (bfl_d3q19_vec.py) is 30x faster than original, making BFL runs feasible on SDAA.
